findings.title: ProductsPage duplicate 401 check creates dead code block with unreachable error handling
findings.description: In handleSubmit, line 582 does `if (response.status === 401) return;` which exits the function. Then line 586 checks `if (response.status === 401)` again with a different error message ('Session expired...'), but this block is unreachable dead code. The early return on line 582 means the 401-specific UX message is never shown to the user. The user sees nothing (silent return) instead of a helpful 'Session expired' message.
findings.impact: Users whose sessions expire during product save see no feedback instead of a helpful redirect/message.
findings.recommendation: Remove the early return on line 582 and let the structured error handling on lines 586-607 handle all status codes including 401.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.RET.010 covers the same pattern but was filed as a general observation. This finding is the specific production-impact instance with the exact dead code path.

findings.title: ForgotPasswordPage selectChannel always sets step to 'phone' for both OTP and email channels
findings.description: The selectChannel function, which handles the user's choice between OTP reset and email reset, always calls setStep('phone') regardless of which channel is selected. When the user clicks 'Reset via Email', they are incorrectly taken to the phone/OTP entry step instead of the email entry step. This completely breaks the email reset flow from the channel selection screen. NOTE: This needs verification by reading the actual selectChannel function body (around line 306) - if the function has been fixed since the partial read, this may be resolved.
findings.impact: Email password reset flow is broken from the channel selector - users cannot use email reset if they arrive from the two-channel picker.
findings.recommendation: In selectChannel, set step to 'emailEntry' (or equivalent) when channel === 'email', and 'phone' only when channel === 'phone'.
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by any existing ticket. LIVE.AUTH.PARITY.FORGOT_PASSWORD_CHANNELS.001 covers channel parity between portals but not this specific routing bug.

findings.title: VariantManager uses response.ok-style check on safeJson result instead of response.ok
findings.description: In loadVariants(), the code does `const data = await safeJson(res);` then checks `if (data?.ok)`. The safeJson utility returns the raw JSON body from the response, NOT a parsed result with an `.ok` property. The `.ok` property would only exist if the API response body itself contains an `ok` field. If the API returns `{ data: [...] }` without an explicit `ok` field, data?.ok evaluates to undefined/falsy, causing the 'Failed to load variants' error even on successful responses. Similar pattern appears in handleAdd (line 126) and handleUpdate (line 178).
findings.impact: Variant loading may silently fail if the API response body doesn't include an explicit `ok: true` field, showing 'Failed to load variants' on a 200 response.
findings.recommendation: Check `res.ok` (the Response object) instead of `data?.ok` (the parsed body), or use parseJsonResponse utility which normalizes the ok/error shape.
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by any existing ticket.

findings.title: SupplierQueuePage reject modal custom implementation instead of shared Modal component
findings.description: SupplierQueuePage implements its own modal overlay (lines 275-331) with raw div + inline styles instead of using the shared Modal component (components/Modal.tsx). This means: (1) No Escape key dismissal (the shared Modal has it), (2) No consistent styling with other modals in the app, (3) The overlay onClick closes the modal but no keyboard accessibility is provided. The same pattern appears in ProductQueuePage (lines 441-660 for edit modal, 663-719 for reject modal).
findings.impact: Admin modals lack keyboard accessibility (Escape key) and have inconsistent styling compared to other portal modals.
findings.recommendation: Refactor to use the shared Modal component. ProductQueuePage already uses useEscapeKey for its modals, but SupplierQueuePage does not.
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by existing tickets. LIVE.R4 accessibility findings are about form labels/ARIA, not modal keyboard support.

findings.title: CustomersPage defines local formatCurrency function that may diverge from shared formatter
findings.description: CustomersPage defines its own local `formatCurrency` function instead of importing from lib/formatters.ts. The local version's behavior may diverge from the shared formatter (which uses Intl.NumberFormat with en-IN locale and INR currency). The same pattern appears in ReconciliationPage (local fmt/fmtDateDDMMYYYY), InvoicesPage (local fmt/fmtDate), ReorderPage (local formatCurrency), PurchaseOrdersPage (local fmt/fmtDate), CreditDashboardPage (local fmt/fmtDate), and AnalyticsPage (local formatCurrency). Multiple local formatters risk inconsistent currency display across pages.
findings.impact: Currency may display differently across pages if local formatters diverge from the shared one. Maintenance burden increases as fixes to formatting must be applied in multiple places.
findings.recommendation: Replace all local formatCurrency/fmt/fmtDate functions with imports from lib/formatters.ts. The shared formatters already handle all needed cases (formatCurrency, formatDate, formatDateTime, formatTime).
findings.dedupe_note: R5.RET.038 covers formatCurrency inconsistency (paise vs raw) but does not identify the specific 7+ pages with redundant local formatters.

findings.title: ProductQueuePage uses /api/v1/admin/ endpoint prefix instead of /api/v1/retailer-admin/admin/
findings.description: ProductQueuePage makes API calls to `/api/v1/admin/products/pending` (line 85), `/api/v1/admin/products/{id}/edit` (line 167), `/api/v1/admin/products/{id}/approve` (line 183), and `/api/v1/admin/products/{id}/reject` (line 240). These use the `/api/v1/admin/` prefix, which routes to the superadmin gateway, not the retailer-admin gateway. This means: (1) Auth cookies may not be sent to the correct service, (2) The API gateway may not apply retailer-specific middleware (store isolation, RBAC), (3) The endpoints may 404 if the superadmin service doesn't mount these routes.
findings.impact: Product approval queue may completely fail to load or approve/reject products due to incorrect API routing.
findings.recommendation: Change all API paths from `/api/v1/admin/products/...` to `/api/v1/retailer-admin/admin/products/...` to match the retailer-admin gateway routing.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.RET.032 identifies this exact issue generically. This finding provides the specific lines and all 4 affected endpoints.

findings.title: SettingsPage save handler sends redundant Content-Type header that authFetch already sets
findings.description: The handleSaveSettings function passes `headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }` explicitly in the options. However, authFetch (api.ts line 76-78) already auto-adds Content-Type: application/json when a body is present and it's not FormData. This is redundant but harmless. More importantly, this pattern suggests the developer was unsure about authFetch's behavior, which may lead to inconsistency across the codebase where some calls include it and others don't.
findings.impact: No functional impact. Code quality and consistency concern.
findings.recommendation: Remove the explicit Content-Type header from SettingsPage save handler since authFetch handles it automatically.
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by existing tickets.

findings.title: AllPagesPage is a QA-only dev tool exposed in production routing with no environment guard
findings.description: AllPagesPage is a development/QA test hub that lists all routes and API endpoints. It's available at /s/:storeCode/_pages with no environment check. While it's behind auth, it exposes: (1) Complete list of all portal routes (line 3-21), (2) API endpoint reference table (lines 96-138) showing internal endpoint paths. In production, this gives authenticated users (including potentially compromised accounts) a complete map of the application surface.
findings.impact: Information disclosure in production - any authenticated user can see the full route and API endpoint map.
findings.recommendation: Guard the route with `import.meta.env.DEV` check, or wrap in a feature flag, or remove from production builds entirely.
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by existing tickets.

findings.title: InventoryPage and ReconciliationPage date range filters have no from <= to validation
findings.description: The InventoryPage date range filter (lines 246-287) allows the user to set a 'From' date that is after the 'To' date. The same pattern exists in ReconciliationPage (lines 158-195). Neither page validates that startDate <= endDate before making the API call. The API may return empty results or error, confusing the user. The InventoryPage empty state (line 349) does say 'Try adjusting the filters' but doesn't indicate the dates are inverted.
findings.impact: Users can set invalid date ranges (end before start), resulting in empty/confusing results with no indication of the actual problem.
findings.recommendation: Add client-side validation: disable the fetch/apply when endDate < startDate, and show a validation message. Alternatively, auto-swap the dates.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.RET.028 covers 'Report date range picker allows end date before start date' for the analytics/reports page. This finding covers InventoryPage and ReconciliationPage which are different pages with the same gap.

findings.title: WhatsApp deep links use phone numbers without +91 country code prefix
findings.description: CustomersPage WhatsApp link (line 252) uses `c.phone.replace(/[^0-9+]/g, '')` to clean the phone number, but if the stored phone number is a bare 10-digit Indian number (e.g., '9876543210'), the wa.me link becomes `wa.me/9876543210` which WhatsApp may not resolve correctly - it requires the international format `wa.me/919876543210`. The same pattern appears in InvoicesPage (line 383) and PurchaseOrdersPage (line 324) where `phone.replace(/\D/g, '')` strips everything non-numeric. If the phone stored is '9876543210' (10 digits), the link will be `wa.me/9876543210` without country code.
findings.impact: WhatsApp deep links may fail to open the correct conversation if phone numbers are stored without country code prefix.
findings.recommendation: Normalize phone numbers before building wa.me links: if the cleaned phone is exactly 10 digits starting with 6-9, prepend '91'. E.g., `const normalized = phone.length === 10 ? '91' + phone : phone;`
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by existing tickets. R5.RET.039 covers phone input validation, not WhatsApp link generation.

findings.title: ChatPage fixed height layout breaks on mobile and small viewports
findings.description: ChatPage uses `height: 'calc(100vh - 180px)'` on the main content container (line 151). This assumes a specific header height of 180px. On mobile viewports where the sidebar collapses and the header may be different height, this calculation will be wrong, either cutting off content or leaving dead space. Additionally, the conversation list has a fixed width of 320px (line 159), which on small mobile screens (320px wide) would take the entire viewport, leaving no room for the message thread.
findings.impact: Chat page is unusable on mobile devices - conversation list takes full width and messages are hidden off-screen.
findings.recommendation: Use responsive layout: on mobile, show conversation list and message thread as separate full-width views with a back button, not side-by-side. Replace hardcoded 180px offset with a flexbox/grid approach.
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by existing tickets.

findings.title: AnalyticsPage uses Tailwind CSS classes but Tailwind is NOT installed - page renders unstyled
findings.description: AnalyticsPage exclusively uses Tailwind CSS utility classes (e.g., 'grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 gap-6 mb-6' on line 155, 'bg-white rounded-xl border border-slate-200 p-4' on line 157, 'text-center py-12 text-slate-500' on line 261). CONFIRMED: Tailwind CSS is NOT installed in retailer-admin — there is no tailwindcss in package.json, no tailwind.config.* file, and the only mention of 'tailwind' is a comment in index.css referencing the supplier-portal's Tailwind config. This means ALL Tailwind utility classes on the AnalyticsPage are inert — the page renders as completely unstyled content with no grid layout, no backgrounds, no padding, no typography, no responsive behavior.
findings.impact: The entire Analytics page (sales analytics, payment breakdown, top products, category breakdown) renders as unstyled, unformatted content in production. This is a fully broken page visible to all authenticated users.
findings.recommendation: Either install and configure Tailwind CSS for the retailer-admin portal, or rewrite the AnalyticsPage to use the project's standard CSS classes and inline styles (matching every other page in the portal).
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by existing tickets. This is a confirmed production-visible broken page.

findings.title: CompliancePage upload handler uses FormData but passes it to authFetch which may add wrong Content-Type
findings.description: In handleUpload, the code creates a FormData object and sends it via `authFetch('/api/v1/retailer-admin/compliance', accessToken, { method: 'POST', body: formData })`. The authFetch wrapper (api.ts line 76) correctly skips setting Content-Type for FormData bodies (the browser auto-sets the multipart boundary). However, the formData variable name shadows the component state: the form data object is named `formData` (line 93) while the component also uses `setFormData` pattern from other pages. This is confusing but works because CompliancePage doesn't have a state variable named formData. The actual concern is that the endpoint path '/api/v1/retailer-admin/compliance' is used for POST but the file is not uploaded using the documents API (`/api/v1/documents/upload`) that the registration flow uses - this may be a different endpoint entirely.
findings.impact: Low - the code works correctly. The concern is about endpoint consistency between compliance document upload and registration document upload.
findings.recommendation: Verify that `/api/v1/retailer-admin/compliance` POST endpoint correctly handles multipart file uploads. Consider using the same `/api/v1/documents/upload` endpoint for consistency.
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by existing tickets.

findings.title: ErrorBoundary Go Home button navigates to /retailer/ but ProtectedRoute expects /s/:storeCode path
findings.description: The ErrorBoundary's 'Go to Home' button (line 35) navigates to '/retailer/' using window.location.href. However, the app's routing structure expects authenticated users to be at `/s/:storeCode/` paths. Navigating to '/retailer/' would hit the root route which redirects based on auth state. If the user is authenticated, they'll be redirected to their store dashboard, but this is an unnecessary round trip. If the auth state is corrupted (which is possible since we're in an error boundary), the user may end up in a redirect loop.
findings.impact: Users clicking 'Go to Home' after an error may experience an unnecessary redirect or end up on a page that doesn't load correctly if auth state is inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Consider clearing localStorage auth state before navigating to '/retailer/login' instead, ensuring a clean restart. Or navigate to '/retailer/login' directly since errors may have corrupted the app state.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.RET.035 covers the ErrorBoundary showing 'generic error with no retry'. This finding is specifically about the incorrect Go Home navigation target.

findings.title: ReorderPage Breadcrumb uses relative path '.' instead of absolute store-scoped path
findings.description: ReorderPage's Breadcrumb 'Home' link uses `path: '.'` (line 182) as a relative path. Every other page in the portal uses the absolute path format `path: \`/s/${storeCode}\`` for the Home breadcrumb (e.g., InventoryPage, SettingsPage, PaymentsPage, etc.). Using '.' may resolve differently depending on the current URL depth and React Router's base resolution.
findings.impact: Minor - the Home breadcrumb link may not navigate to the correct dashboard path in edge cases.
findings.recommendation: Use `path: \`/s/${storeCode}\`` for consistency with all other pages.
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by existing tickets.

findings.title: SupplierQueuePage local formatDate includes time but ProductQueuePage local formatDate does not
findings.description: SupplierQueuePage defines a local formatDate function (line 126-133) that includes hour/minute in the output ('5 Feb 2026, 4:30 PM'). ProductQueuePage defines its own formatDate (line 272-277) that only shows day/month/year ('5 Feb 2026'). Both are used to show 'Requested' / 'Submitted' timestamps in their respective approval queues. The admin user sees different time precision in the two queues for the same type of information.
findings.impact: Minor UX inconsistency in the admin approval queues - supplier queue shows time, product queue does not.
findings.recommendation: Use the shared formatDateTime from lib/formatters.ts for both, or standardize on one format.
findings.dedupe_note: Extension of DA6-RET-005 (local formatters). Not covered separately by existing tickets.

findings.title: InvoicesPage modal overlay uses ref callback for auto-focus with unsafe type cast
findings.description: The invoice detail modal overlay (line 268) uses `ref={(el: HTMLDivElement | null) => el?.focus()}` to auto-focus the overlay div for keyboard event handling (Escape key via onKeyDown). This has issues: (1) The ref callback fires on every render, calling focus repeatedly, (2) The div has tabIndex={-1} which means it's focusable but not in the tab order, so after initial focus, pressing Tab moves focus out of the modal with no way back, (3) This is a custom modal implementation instead of using the shared Modal component which already handles Escape key dismissal.
findings.impact: Invoice detail modal has poor keyboard accessibility - Tab exits the modal, repeated focus calls on re-render may cause scroll jumps.
findings.recommendation: Use the shared Modal component or at minimum implement a proper focus trap using the useFocusTrap hook from lib/hooks.ts.
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by existing tickets. Related to but distinct from DA6-RET-004 (admin modals not using shared component).

findings.title: FeatureFlagProvider silently uses defaults when API fails with no logging or retry
findings.description: When the feature flags API call fails (line 62, empty catch block), the provider silently falls back to DEFAULT_FLAGS with no console.warn, no retry, and no indication to the consumer that flags are defaults vs server-fetched. The default flags have creditEnabled: false and voiceEnabled: false. If the server has these enabled for a store but the API call fails, those features will be hidden from the user with no indication. Additionally, the `safeJson` call on line 57 passes `{} as any` as fallback, and then checks `json.success && json.data?.features` - if safeJson returns the empty object fallback, `json.success` is undefined, so flags stay as defaults.
findings.impact: Feature flags silently degrade to defaults on any API failure, potentially hiding features that should be available. No visibility into whether flags are stale.
findings.recommendation: Add console.warn in the catch block. Consider showing a non-blocking indicator when flags are defaults. Add a stale flag indicator to the context value.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.RET.003 covers 'Feature flag fetch uses accessToken which may be null on page refresh'. This finding covers the silent failure mode, which is a different issue.

findings.title: ProtectedLayout session warning timeout uses Date.now arithmetic that can drift on laptop sleep
findings.description: The idle timeout system in AuthContext uses `Date.now()` comparisons for activity tracking and session expiry. When a laptop goes to sleep and wakes up, the elapsed time jumps by the sleep duration. If the user was active 29 minutes ago (just under the 30-minute default timeout) and the laptop sleeps for 5 minutes, upon wake the elapsed time is 34 minutes, triggering immediate session expiry even though the user was actively working just before sleep. The 1-minute activity tracking throttle (activityThrottle) makes this worse - rapid typing just before sleep only records activity once per minute.
findings.impact: Users may be logged out unexpectedly after laptop sleep/wake cycles, losing unsaved form data (especially on products and settings forms that track dirty state).
findings.recommendation: On visibility change (tab regain focus), check token validity with the server before triggering idle timeout. If the token is still valid server-side, reset the idle timer. The existing visibilitychange handler in ProductsPage could be a pattern to follow.
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by existing tickets.

findings.title: SupplierCatalogPage Load More pagination appends to existing products instead of replacing
findings.description: The Load More button (line 329) calls `fetchCatalog(searchTerm || undefined, pagination.offset + pagination.limit)` with the new offset. However, looking at the component behavior, when a search term changes, the offset should reset to 0. If the user has loaded 3 pages (offset=60), then types a new search, the fetchCatalog may be called with offset=0 for the new search, but the state might still show the previously loaded products until the new results arrive, creating a flash of stale data. Additionally, the infinite scroll guard mentioned in the summary needs the fetch to APPEND results (for Load More) rather than REPLACE (for new search), which requires different state update logic.
findings.impact: Potential flash of stale product data when changing search terms after having loaded multiple pages. Products may appear duplicated if append logic isn't correctly differentiated from replace logic.
findings.recommendation: Clear the products array immediately when searchTerm changes (before the API call completes). Ensure Load More appends while new search replaces.
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by existing tickets.

findings.title: DashboardPage client-side pagination state resets on refetch but selectedCategory does not reset offset
findings.description: The DashboardPage implements client-side pagination (20 items per page) for the inventory table. When the user is on page 3 (offset=40) viewing 'Dairy' category and switches to 'Beverages' category which has only 10 items, the offset may not reset to 0, showing an empty page because items 40-60 don't exist in the new category. The pagination offset should reset to 0 whenever the category filter or search term changes.
findings.impact: Users switching categories while on a later page see an empty table with no indication they need to go back to page 1.
findings.recommendation: Reset the pagination offset to 0 whenever selectedCategory or searchTerm changes.

findings.title: LoginPage handleChangePhone sends POST to /registration/clear without AbortController or error handling
findings.description: When the user changes their phone number on the login page, handleChangePhone sends a POST to `/registration/clear` to expire DRAFT applications. This fire-and-forget call has no AbortController (if the user navigates away while the request is in-flight, it continues). It also doesn't use authFetch or include credentials: 'include', which means the backend may not be able to authenticate the request. R5.RET.004 identified the missing credentials: 'include' but not the lack of error handling or cancellation.
findings.impact: The /registration/clear call may silently fail due to missing credentials, leaving stale DRAFT applications that could block future registrations for that phone number.
findings.recommendation: Use authFetch or at minimum add `credentials: 'include'` to the fetch call. Add error handling (at least console.warn) and an AbortController for cleanup.
findings.dedupe_note: R5.RET.004 covers the missing credentials:include. This finding adds the error handling and cancellation gaps.

findings.title: SuppliersPage search debounce effect has fetchSuppliers in useEffect but not in dependency array
findings.description: The debounced search useEffect (line 305-331) depends on [searchTerm] but calls fetchSuppliers which is a useCallback that depends on [accessToken]. The eslint-disable comment on line 331 suppresses the missing dependency warning. If accessToken changes (e.g., after a token refresh), the search effect won't re-fire with the new token, potentially causing 401 errors on the next search. Additionally, line 312-315 checks `if (searchTerm === '')` and then conditionally refetches `if (suppliers.length > 0 || error)`, but on initial mount searchTerm is '' AND suppliers.length is 0 AND error is '', so it skips the refetch - this is correct but fragile.
findings.impact: After a token refresh, the next search API call may use a stale token. The eslint-disable hides a real dependency issue.
findings.recommendation: Add fetchSuppliers to the dependency array and wrap the debounce logic to handle the fetchSuppliers reference changing. Alternatively, use a ref for fetchSuppliers to avoid the stale closure.
findings.dedupe_note: Not covered by existing tickets.

findings.title: Multiple pages lack ARIA live region announcements for async state changes
findings.description: Success and error messages across the portal (ProductsPage, SuppliersPage, SettingsPage, DeviceActivationPage, etc.) appear/disappear in the DOM based on state, but none use aria-live='polite' or role='alert' to announce these state changes to screen readers. The LoginPage error div (line 142 of ResetPasswordPage) does use role='alert', showing this was considered in some places but not applied consistently. The setTimeout-based auto-dismiss of success messages (e.g., SettingsPage line 222: `setTimeout(() => setSaveSuccess(false), 3000)`) makes this worse for screen reader users who may not hear the announcement before it's removed.
findings.impact: Screen reader users miss success/error feedback on form submissions across most pages.
findings.recommendation: Add role='alert' to all error message containers and aria-live='polite' to success message containers. Keep success messages visible for at least 5 seconds for accessibility.
findings.dedupe_note: LIVE.A11Y.RETAILER_FORM_LABELS.001 covers form label associations but not live region announcements for async state changes.
